jobs.name: Night Shift — Scout Run (23:00 IST)
jobs.prompt:
Execute the Night Shift Scout Run exactly as specified in the playbook at `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\01-scout-run.md`. 

Your mission: Intake raw captures, classify them, and prepare for refinement. You are the gatekeeper.

CRITICAL: Read these files first before taking any action:
1. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\house-rules.md` — the Prime Directive (NO SOURCE, NO NOTE)
2. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\01-scout-run.md` — the full Scout protocol
3. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\07 - SYSTEM\index.md` — current vault structure

Then execute the 5-step Scout Pipeline:
1. INTAKE SCAN: Check `00 INBOX/` and `0-raw/` for new material since last run
2. CLASSIFICATION: For each item, determine type (article/book/paper/video/idea), extract metadata (title, author, date, source URL), create literature note in `1-desk/<subtype>/` with proper frontmatter
3. PRIME DIRECTIVE GATE: Verify every item has a verifiable source. Items without sources go to `1-desk/_quarantine/` with `status: quarantined`. No interpretation — summaries are extractive only.
4. SAVE: Use naming convention `YYYY-MM-DD — [Title].md`. Preserve source URLs verbatim.
5. LOG & REPORT: Append to `night-shift-log.md` with format: `## [YYYY-MM-DD 23:XX] Scout Run | Processed N items`. Do NOT create a morning brief — that is handled separately.

If nothing new is found, log: "Scout: 0 new items (vault intake clean)" and stop.

Vault path: E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault

jobs.name: Night Shift — Refinery Run (03:00 IST)
jobs.prompt:
Execute the Night Shift Refinery Run exactly as specified in the playbook at `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\02-refinery-run.md`.

Your mission: Extract atomic notes from literature notes in `1-desk/`. One idea → one file. No interpretation, no drift.

CRITICAL: Read these files first before taking any action:
1. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\house-rules.md` — the Prime Directive
2. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\02-refinery-run.md` — the full Refinery protocol
3. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\07 - SYSTEM\ai-first-rules.md` — frontmatter standards

Then execute the 5-step Refinery Pipeline:
1. SOURCE VERIFICATION: For each literature note in `1-desk/` with `status: to-process`, verify the source exists. Skip quarantined or already-processed items.
2. ATOMIC EXTRACTION: Extract one idea per file. Own words only. Source citation mandatory. No additions. Every atom gets frontmatter with `date`, `type: permanent`, `tags`, `ai-first: true`, `source`.
3. NAMING: Atomic titles like `Concept Name.md` (no date prefix). Save to `2-atoms/`.
4. SOURCE ARCHIVAL: Move processed literature notes to `sources/archived/`. Update frontmatter to `status: processed`.
5. LOG: Append to `night-shift-log.md` with format: `## [YYYY-MM-DD 03:XX] Refinery Run | Extracted N atoms`.

If no literature notes with `status: to-process` exist, log: "Refinery: 0 items to process" and stop.

For friction detection: If a new claim contradicts an existing vault note, create a `[FRICTION]` block in `3-threads/_friction/` following the template in the playbook.

jobs.name: Night Shift — Editor Run (06:00 IST)
jobs.prompt:
Execute the Night Shift Editor Run exactly as specified in the playbook at `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\03-editor-run.md`.

Your mission: Link atomic notes into a knowledge graph, detect contradictions, and update the vault index. You are the cartographer.

CRITICAL: Read these files first before taking any action:
1. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\house-rules.md` — Prime Directive & friction system
2. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\03-editor-run.md` — the full Editor protocol
3. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\07 - SYSTEM\index.md` — current vault structure

Then execute the 5-step Editor Pipeline:
1. LINK NEW ATOMS: For each new atom from last Refinery Run, add 2+ outgoing wikilinks and ensure 1+ incoming backlink from existing notes. Search vault for related concepts, people, projects.
2. FRICTION DETECTION: Scan for contradictions between new atoms and existing vault knowledge. Create `[FRICTION]` blocks in `3-threads/_friction/`. NEVER resolve them — only flag for morning review.
3. UPDATE INDEX: Add new atoms to `07 - SYSTEM/index.md` under appropriate sections.
4. LOG: Append to `night-shift-log.md` with format: `## [YYYY-MM-DD 06:XX] Editor Run | Linked N atoms, flagged F conflicts`.
5. ORPHAN CHECK: Scan for notes with 0 incoming links (7+ days old). Report in `3-threads/orphans/`.

If no new atoms exist, log: "Editor: 0 new atoms to link" and stop.

Then create/append the morning brief at `BRIEFINGS/YYYY-MM-DD — Morning Brief.md` with all three run summaries (Scout, Refinery, Editor).

jobs.name: Night Shift — Audit Run (Sun 22:00 IST)
jobs.prompt:
Execute the Night Shift Audit Run exactly as specified in the playbook at `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\04-audit-run.md`.

Your mission: Weekly vault health sweep — find rot, stale claims, broken links, and quality drift. You are the inspector.

CRITICAL: Read these files first before taking any action:
1. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\house-rules.md` — Quality Gates & enforcement
2. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\playbooks\04-audit-run.md` — the full Audit protocol
3. `E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\07 - SYSTEM\index.md` — current vault structure

Then execute the 7-step Audit Pipeline:
1. VAULT HEALTH SCAN: Check for duplicates, orphans (0 incoming links, 7+ days old), broken wikilinks, missing frontmatter. Generate a health report with overall score at `3-threads/_audit/YYYY-MM-DD — Vault Health.md`.
2. STALE CLAIM DETECTION: Scan for time-sensitive claims >6 months old without recency markers ("as of YYYY-MM"). Flag role claims (CEO, founder) as HIGH priority, funding numbers as HIGH, general facts as LOW.
3. QUALITY SAMPLING: Spot-check 10-15 random atoms from `2-atoms/`, `02 - PERMANENT/concepts/`, and `wiki/concepts/`. Check each for source citation, "For future Claude" preamble, 2+ wikilinks, confidence marker. Calculate quality score (target: 95%+).
4. BROKEN LINK CLEANUP: For each broken wikilink, create stubs in `3-threads/_stubs/`. Do NOT delete links — flag for morning review.
5. WEEKLY SYNTHESIS: Look for concept co-occurrence patterns. If 3+ notes share a new theme, create a synthesis note in `05 - MAPS/`.
6. UPDATE DASHBOARD: Append weekly metrics to `07 - SYSTEM/audit-dashboard.md` (create if missing).
7. LOG: Append to `night-shift-log.md` with format: `## [YYYY-MM-DD 22:XX] Audit Run | Week YYYY-WNN | Score: XX/100`.

IMPORTANT: Never fix issues yourself — flag them for morning review. Never delete orphaned notes. Never "correct" content — only flag.

jobs.name: History Watchdog — Weekly Scout (Mon 02:00 IST)
jobs.prompt:
Execute the History Watchdog Scout Run for this week.

## Your Mission
Run curated research queries across 4 domains (Aryan migration, Dravidian politics, RSS/Hindutva funding, anti-caste movements) using free AI research tools. Output a structured JSON report for human review.

## Setup
- Vault: E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault
- Queries file: E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\03 - PROJECTS\History-Watchdog\queries.yaml
- Output: E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\03 - PROJECTS\History-Watchdog\raw\YYYY-MM-DD-scout.json
- Working directory: E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault

## Step 1 — Read queries.yaml
Use read_file to load E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\03 - PROJECTS\History-Watchdog\queries.yaml
This contains 24 queries across 4 categories. Prioritize critical queries first.

## Step 2 — Run searches
For each query category, use browser_navigate to access free tools:

**Elicit.org** (elicit.org): Academic paper search — navigate, search each query, collect paper titles/authors/abstracts/venues/publication years.

**Undermind.ai** (undermind.ai): Deep academic search — navigate, search each query, collect findings with reasoning chains.

**DeepSeek Deep Research** (chat.deepseek.com): Web search + structured reports — navigate to chat.deepseek.com, start deep research mode, run queries, collect structured output.

**Kimi** (kimi.com): Long document summarization — use for any papers >10 pages found in other searches.

For each query:
1. Navigate to the tool
2. Run the search
3. Collect: title, authors, year, venue, abstract (or executive summary for web sources)
4. Note which tool produced it

## Step 3 — Compile results
Create a JSON file at E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\03 - PROJECTS\History-Watchdog\raw\2026-07-14-scout.json (use today's date)

Format:
```json
{
  "run_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "queries_run": N,
  "papers_found": N,
  "by_category": {
    "aryan_migration": { "queries": N, "papers": N, "top_papers": [...] },
    "dravidian_politics": { "queries": N, "papers": N, "top_papers": [...] },
    "rss_hindutva": { "queries": N, "papers": N, "top_papers": [...] },
    "anti_caste": { "queries": N, "papers": N, "top_papers": [...] }
  },
  "tier1_papers": [...],
  "notes": "any issues, tools that failed, queries that returned nothing"
}
```

Prioritize tier1 venue papers (Science, Cell, Nature, PNAS, AJHG, Current Biology, PLOS Genetics).

## Step 4 — Log to history-watchdog/logs/
Append a brief entry to E:\_Knowledge\ObsidianVault\03 - PROJECTS\History-Watchdog\logs\YYYY-MM-DD-run-log.md

## Rules
- Use web search for all queries — DO NOT fabricate paper titles or abstracts
- If a tool is unavailable, note it and continue with others
- Collect at minimum: title, authors, year, venue/source, 1-sentence summary
- Output must be REAL data from live searches — no placeholders
- Save to the JSON file even if some queries fail
